questions.originalText: Jivuba's renunciation and disinterest in married life.
questions.answer: Jivuba demonstrated remarkable renunciation and disinterest in married life from a young age. Despite being married to Hathiya Patgar of Kundal due to her father's insistence, she remained focused on bhakti and spiritual life. She openly told her mother-in-law Raibai that she wished to remain celibate and worship God. Through Raibai's understanding and convincing, Jivuba received written permission from her husband to pursue her spiritual calling and returned to Gadhada. Even after marriage, she maintained strict vows like sleeping on the floor, staying away from material pleasures, and giving up the six different types of tastes. Both she and her sister Laduba, though married, lived according to celibate rules of sadhus and had vows not to look at men other than Maharaj, showing complete dedication to spiritual life over worldly married obligations.

questions.answer: The scriptural debate with Khaiyo Khatri was a significant event where Bhagwan Swaminarayan instructed Brahmanand Swami to sit in His place on the seat while He sat on the ground nearby. This was a strategic arrangement where Maharaj, while appearing as a humble disciple, would actually conduct the debate. Brahmanand Swami was initially hesitant to take Maharaj's place as it meant playing the role of God, but he was helpless against Maharaj's command.

questions.answer: Jhinabhai demonstrated deep love and affection for God's devotees in several ways. He had much love for Maharaj (Bhagwan Swaminarayan) and showed great care for female devotees like Jivuba and other women living in Gadhada. When Maharaj was planning to travel to Panchala, Jhinabhai insisted on bringing the female devotees along, even though it was not Maharaj's wish. Despite Maharaj wanting the women to stay back, Jhinabhai gathered all the female devotees and took them to Panchala, showing his concern for their spiritual welfare and desire to include them in the divine company. His obstinate insistence on bringing them, though it disappointed Maharaj initially, reflected his deep affection and care for ensuring all devotees could benefit from being in the presence of God. However, this same love could sometimes manifest as stubbornness, which Maharaj sought to correct through his teachings.

questions.answer: Nirgundas Swami made significant contributions to spreading satsang through his unwavering dedication and outreach efforts. He was always by Shastriji Maharaj's side during satsang activities and played a crucial role in preventing people from falling away from satsang. His primary methods included: 1) Actively reaching out to anyone who fell back from satsang without fail, 2) Speaking to them about the greatness of Purushottam and Shastriji Maharaj through talks based on the Vachanamrut and other satsang shastras, 3) Constantly working to keep devotees engaged, as seen with his efforts in Khandesh where devotees became engrossed in Swamishri due to his constant efforts, and 4) Despite his own greatness, always directing devotees toward Swamishri rather than drawing them to himself. His dedication was so complete that he would undertake missions at Swamishri's behest, such as attempting to bring Radharamanprasad from Chhapaiya, demonstrating his commitment to expanding the satsang community.
